referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A fixed shrine: the doors are moulded shut at two draw calls and nothing turns or swings; the offerings are a separate asset, so nothing attaches here and there are no sockets. One root pivot. At the corner of every plot, shop and hotel forecourt. Weathered grey cast stone, gilt paint flaking to verdigris, dark blue-black brick-lattice panels, a pair of little doors.

reasoning: ONE stone merge -- an 8-segment moulded base lathe, a round stem lathe, a square slab -- and ONE gold merge -- the body box, four lattice plates, two doors with lattice, four corner posts, a plinth, two hip-roof lathes at 4 segments yawed 45 degrees, a finial lathe and four curled eave tubes: TWO draw calls of 2.

Two materials: grey stone (vertex colours: two stones) and gilt (vertex colours: gold, dark gold, near-black lattice), each with a grime canvas -- the plate's verdigris flecks on the gold ride the canvas.
No repetition system: four eave curls are four short tubes in the merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the flared roof with upturned corners over a small gilt box on a stone pedestal; the roof is a 4-segment lathe with a concave profile so it flares without a sculpted surface, and the lattice is a dark plate because a brick grid is below the resolvable band.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.63 x 1.30 x 0.62 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: An octagonal moulded base 0.551 wide to 0.24, a round stem to 0.335, a two-tier slab (0.555 plinth to 0.415, 0.434 riser to 0.513); a 0.425 x 0.415 gilt body to 0.838 with lattice panels and doors on +Z; a flared square roof 0.575 across the flats at 0.854 rising to a ridge at 1.016, its four eave edges swept up into corner horns reaching 0.637 across; an upper roof to 1.146 and a lotus finial to 1.30.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x +-0.3166 and z +-0.3086 at the UPSWEPT EAVE CORNERS, which are what the envelope is for: a 4-segment roof lathe yawed 45 degrees puts its square's corners at the bbox extremes, and the horn tips add their outward run and 24 mm fascia radius on top of the 0.575 m eave plane. y 0 to 1.30 (declared). The declaration was corrected 0.50 x 0.45 -> 0.63 x 0.62 at model time; the old 0.50 could not hold the model's OWN pedestal, which measured 0.551 m across. Proxy occupancy (w:h:d 1:2.057:1.001): base 0-0.14 H full width, stem 0.18-0.30, slab 0.26-0.34 full width, body 0.34-0.62 H at 0.70 W, eave zone 0.66-0.74 H full width, upper roof 0.78-0.86 at 0.36 W, finial 0.90-0.98 -- built as base to 0.16, stem 0.16-0.36, slab 0.36-0.44, body 0.44-0.86, eave 0.87-0.98, ridge 1.08, upper roof 1.09-1.20, finial to 1.30. The ten-band proxy comparison now reads mean |delta w| 0.0054 and |delta d| 0.0047 of H with every band inside 0.015, against 0.0386 / 0.0523 for the first build. Three separate faults were behind that: the declared envelope was 0.50 where the proxy needs 0.63; the roof eave was 0.52 across the flats where band 6 reads 0.442 H = 0.575; and the slab was ONE box, which cannot be both band 2 (0.427 H = 0.555 m) and band 3 (0.334 H = 0.434 m) -- it is a moulded two-tier plinth and riser, which is also what the plate shows.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1:2.057:1.001, 1,942 triangles. Band table after the third build: mean |delta width| 0.039, |delta depth| 0.052 of height; the roof band came within 0.035 once the eave was built as the proxy's 0.1 m thick band rather than an edge.

featureReviews.notes: THE EAVE IS A CONTINUOUS ROLLED FASCIA, NOT FOUR CORNER STUBS. The plate (scratch/_horn.png, the plate's left eave corner at 3x) shows the eave EDGE dipping at mid-span and sweeping up into a point at each corner -- one curve, not a brim with horns bolted on. The first build had four 12 mm tubes of three points each at the corners of a straight-edged pyramid, which is why the single most recognisable feature of a spirit house was absent from the silhouette. Each of the four eave edges is now one 24 mm swept tube through seven stations: tip out and up, knee at the corner, a -22 mm dip at mid-span, mirrored. Two tube ends meet at every corner, which is correct -- the horn IS thicker than the fascia either side of it. The tips then taper 24 mm -> 7 mm over their last two stations: `tube` caps every segment, so a constant radius ends the horn in a flat disc and it rendered as four cut-off posts.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout: two components at 2 draw calls of 2; pedestal and house at stations re-derived from the plate row scan (739 px/m) and checked band by band against the proxy.

Band table: all ten bands under-width, mean |delta w| 0.0386 of H. The cause is the DECLARATION, not the build -- the proxy's widest band is 0.442 H = 0.575 m and the asset declared 0.50, which the model's own octagonal pedestal (0.551 m across) already stood outside. Declared size corrected to 0.63 x 1.30 x 0.62 with the arithmetic recorded in notes.

Pedestal 0.062 m over the corrected envelope: HD is a lathe RADIUS at seg 8 ry PI/8, so its flats sit at HD*cos(22.5), and it had been set as though it were a width. HD 0.332 -> 0.298 to land band 0 on the proxy's 0.426 H.
Bands 2 and 3 traded 0.031 under for 0.050 over. One slab box cannot be both 0.555 m and 0.434 m: split into a moulded plinth and riser and dropped 32 mm. Residual 0.0117/0.0112 -> 0.0054/0.0047.

reviewHistory.summary: Structural pass. The band table found three structural faults and the declared envelope was one of them: the proxy needs 0.63 x 0.62 where the asset declared 0.50 x 0.45, which the model's own 0.551 m pedestal already exceeded. Declaration corrected with the arithmetic in notes; roof eave widened to the measured 0.575 across the flats; the slab split into a moulded plinth and riser because one box cannot be both band 2 (0.555) and band 3 (0.434). Ten-band residual 0.0386/0.0523 -> 0.0054/0.0047 of H.

The first eave horns rendered as four vertical FLAGPOLES: three points each, with the tip 87 mm above the corner over 9 mm of outward run. A horn is mostly outward travel with the lift spread over the last third of the edge; rebuilt at seven stations per edge so the whole eave curves rather than turning a corner.

The rebuilt horns still ended in flat discs -- `tube` caps every segment, so a constant radius cannot come to a point and they read as cut-off posts. `tube` now takes one radius per station (a plain number is byte-identical: verified against police-traffic-barrier at max |diff| 0 over 1,140 vertices), and each tip tapers 24 mm -> 7 mm.

featureReviews.evidence: Eave plane 0.575 m across the flats (proxy band 6 = 0.442 H), concave flared profile to a ridge at 1.016, a second tier to 1.146, a lotus finial to 1.30. Bands 6 and 7 now +0.004 / +0.011 against -0.038 / -0.026.
featureReviews.notes: THE EAVE IS A CONTINUOUS ROLLED FASCIA, NOT FOUR CORNER STUBS. The plate (scratch/_horn.png, the plate's left eave corner at 3x) shows the eave EDGE dipping at mid-span and sweeping up into a point at each corner -- one curve, not a brim with horns bolted on. The first build had four 12 mm tubes of three points each at the corners of a straight-edged pyramid, which is why the single most recognisable feature of a spirit house was absent from the silhouette. Each of the four eave edges is now one 24 mm swept tube through seven stations: tip out and up, knee at the corner, a -22 mm dip at mid-span, mirrored. Two tube ends meet at every corner, which is correct -- the horn IS thicker than the fascia either side of it. The tips then taper 24 mm -> 7 mm over their last two stations: `tube` caps every segment, so a constant radius ends the horn in a flat disc and it rendered as four cut-off posts.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 1,624/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/8 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases. The eave rebuild cost 224 triangles and no other axis; the horn taper and the heavier verdigris cost nothing on any of the four.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components, no repetition system: 2 of 2.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 892 of 2,000: an 8-segment and a 12-segment lathe, two 4-segment roof lathes, a 10-segment finial, sixteen boxes, four tubes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Lathes for the base, stem, roofs and finial; boxes for the slab, body, panels, doors, posts; tubes for the eave curls.
No InstancedMesh: four eave curls are one merge. In a scene the HOST instances the shrine.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two 256 px grime canvases after construction, 0.5 MB.
